plan:
-   **Electronics**: ESP32 (flight controller/telemetry), Brushless DC motors, ESCs, LiPo battery with PDB, IMU sensor (accelerometer/gyro), RC receiver (or WiFi control module).
-   **Structure**: Modular frame (carbon fiber, aluminum, or 3D-printed sections), Propellers, Landing gear, Vibration dampeners.
-   **Custom Parts**: 3D-printed mounts for ESP32 and IMU, modular interlocking frame components, battery tray, camera mount if FPV is desired.
-   **Assembly**: Standardized connectors for easy swapping of modules (e.g., JST, XT30/60), quick-release mechanisms for arms or payload bays.
-   **Software**: Custom firmware for ESP32 or adaptation of existing open-source flight control software (e.g., INAV/ArduPilot-based for ESP32).
-   **Power Management**: Dedicated voltage regulators for ESP32 and peripherals, battery monitoring circuit.

subSteps.title: 3D print all specified mechanical components
Clean and deburr all 3D printed parts for smooth fitment
Test fit motors into motor mounts and ESCs into ESC mounts
Test fit flight controller, IMU, PDB, and RC receiver into their respective mounts/trays
Solder motor phase wires to ESC motor outputs
Solder LiPo battery main leads to Power Distribution Board (PDB) input
Solder ESC power input leads to PDB motor outputs
Solder PDB 5V outputs to 5V voltage regulator input, then regulator output to Flight Controller, IMU, and RC Receiver
Wire ESC PWM signal inputs to Flight Controller PWM outputs
Wire IMU I2C (SCL/SDA) and power lines to Flight Controller I2C port
Wire RC Receiver serial (iBUS) output and power lines to Flight Controller UART RX port
Perform continuity check on all soldered power connections to prevent shorts
Connect Flight Controller to computer and flash appropriate drone firmware (e.g., Betaflight, ArduPilot)
Verify Flight Controller is recognized by the configuration software and basic settings are applied
Calibrate IMU sensor and verify correct orientation and sensor readings in software
Bind RC Receiver to transmitter and verify channel outputs are correctly registered by the Flight Controller
Perform initial ESC calibration and motor direction tests (without propellers for safety)
Configure flight modes, PID settings, and safety features in Flight Controller software
Attach arms and landing skids to the central frame plate using M3 screws and nuts
Mount motor mounts and motors to the arms, and secure ESC mounts to the arms with zip ties/adhesive
Mount the PDB, 5V regulator, FC tray, IMU mount, RC receiver mount, and battery strap holder to the central frame plate with standoffs and screws
Install LiPo battery strap through the battery strap holder and secure LiPo battery to the frame
Route and secure all wiring with zip ties, ensuring no cables interfere with moving parts or propellers
Attach propellers to the motors, ensuring correct CW/CCW rotation as per motor direction tests
Attach payload module base plate to central frame (if applicable)
Perform a final visual inspection and system-level functional test (hover test) in a safe environment

projectDescription: This modular drone features an ESP32 as its primary flight controller, integrating an IMU, brushless motors, ESCs, and a LiPo battery for propulsion. Its design allows for easily interchangeable frame sections and various payload modules, emphasizing versatility.

imagePromptSnapshot.description:
Project idea: 帮我设计一款无人机,要求模块化,最好用esp32

Design notes: modular design, ESP32 primary controller, drone platform

Electrical components (current): Main Flight Controller (mcu, 52x28x13mm); IMU Sensor (sensor, 15x25x3mm); 4x actuator: Front Left Motor, Front Right Motor, Rear Left Motor, Rear Right Motor; 5x module: Front Left ESC, Front Right ESC, Rear Left ESC, Rear Right ESC +1 more; 3x power: Main LiPo Battery, Power Distribution Board, 5V Voltage Regulator for FC/Peripherals

Mechanical/structural parts (current): 6x structural: Central Frame Plate, Front Left Arm, Front Right Arm, Rear Left Arm +2 more; 15x 3d_printed: Front Left Motor Mount, Front Right Motor Mount, Rear Left Motor Mount, Rear Right Motor Mount +11 more; 4x mechanism: Front Left CW Propeller, Front Right CCW Propeller, Rear Left CCW Propeller, Rear Right CW Propeller; 5x misc: LiPo Battery Strap, M3x10mm Standoffs, M3x6mm Screws, M2x5mm Screws +1 more

Assembly: Central Frame Plate → Front Left Arm (M3 bolts); Central Frame Plate → Front Right Arm (M3 bolts); Central Frame Plate → Rear Left Arm (M3 bolts); Central Frame Plate → Rear Right Arm (M3 bolts); Central Frame Plate → Front Landing Skid (M3 bolts); Central Frame Plate → Rear Landing Skid (M3 bolts); Central Frame Plate → Flight Controller Mount Tray (M3 bolts and standoffs); Central Frame Plate → PDB Mount (M3 bolts and standoffs); Central Frame Plate → Battery Strap Holder (M3 bolts); Central Frame Plate → RC Receiver Mount (M2 screws); Central Frame Plate → Payload Module Base Plate (quick release/M3 bolts); Front Left Arm → Front Left Motor Mount (M2 screws); Front Left Arm → Front Left ESC Mount (zip ties/adhesive); Front Right Arm → Front Right Motor Mount (M2 screws); Front Right Arm → Front Right ESC Mount (zip ties/adhesive) (+19 more connections)

tools: Heat gun or lighter (for heat shrink)
assumptions: Basic understanding of drone components and their function.
Familiarity with 3D printing processes and post-processing.
Competent in basic through-hole and surface-mount soldering techniques.
Access to a computer with a USB port for flashing firmware.
Knowledge of drone flight controller firmware (e.g., Betaflight, ArduPilot) and configuration software.
